text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Eating disorders psychiatry consultation in one week to confirm the diagnosis, decide the level of care, and lead a multidisciplinary plan
  • Medical assessment and stabilization: orthostatic vital signs and temperature, ECG, blood count, electrolytes with phosphate and magnesium, glucose, kidney and liver tests, albumin, TSH, CRP, ferritin and vitamin D; admission criteria explained; electrolytes, phosphate and magnesium to be rechecked three to four days after the meal plan starts, then weekly for the first weeks
  • Refeeding risk: thiamine 100 mg daily before and during the first two weeks, and a starting meal plan of about 1,600 kcal a day in three meals and two snacks, increased by about 200 to 300 kcal every few days
  • Collaborative safety plan with warning signs, coping steps, people to contact including her travelling companion, the clinic number, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and local emergency numbers abroad; medicines dispensed in small supplies and kept by her companion
  • Privacy: the chart is flagged as restricted, access is audited, she is booked under a scheduling alias at the first or last appointment of the day, and weights are discussed only in the consulting room
  • Multidisciplinary outpatient treatment: weekly CBT-E with an eating disorders therapist, a dietitian twice a month, medical review by the primary clinician, and psychiatry review; open weighing at sessions instead of weighing at home; by video when she travels
  • Compulsive exercise: no gymnastics and walks of no more than an hour a day while weight is restored and the pulse and orthostatic changes are abnormal, with a graded return agreed by the team
  • Bone health: DXA of the spine and hip, calcium 1,200 mg a day from food and supplement, vitamin D, weight restoration as the main treatment, and repeat DXA in two years
  • Depression with persistent grief: grief-focused work within therapy; sertraline 25 mg daily, increased to 50 mg after two weeks, once nutrition was under way and the QTc was normal; PHQ-9 at every visit and suicide-risk review at every visit

resource.title: Elisabeth of Austria synthetic care plan
resource.description: Recognizing and managing a restrictive eating disorder in a 56-year-old woman who presents with weight loss, fatigue, ankle swelling and dizziness, with compulsive exercise and frequent self-weighing since early adulthood: DSM-5-TR anorexia nervosa, restricting type, in later life; medical stabilization under the APA 2023 guideline, the SAHM 2022 medical management paper (written for younger patients and applied with care), the AED medical care standards and the ASPEN refeeding consensus (orthostatic vital signs, ECG for bradycardia and QTc, electrolytes with phosphate and magnesium, glucose, thiamine before nutrition, refeeding risk, and admission thresholds); bone density by DXA; a multidisciplinary team with an eating disorders psychiatrist, a dietitian and CBT-E; recurrent depression with persistent grief, with a structured safety assessment and a safety plan; a gastroenteritis that threatens potassium and the QTc on sertraline; preventive care at 56; the privacy of a public figure; and continuity of care for a patient who travels for weeks at a time.

Bone health: DXA of the spine and hip, calcium 1,200 mg a day from food and supplement, vitamin D, weight restoration as the main treatment, and repeat DXA in two years

Depression with persistent grief: grief-focused work within therapy; sertraline 25 mg daily, increased to 50 mg after two weeks, once nutrition was under way and the QTc was normal; PHQ-9 at every visit and suicide-risk review at every visit
